title: Ig-Seq/Rep-Seq/MAF
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic and explicitly supported method variants. One RNA-derived immunoglobulin target route is drawn: reverse transcription with a UID-bearing primer, second-strand synthesis with a second UID-bearing primer, PCR, then purification to DNA. The catalogue identifies the drawing as MAF; primary-paper interpretation is restricted to Khan et al.'s mouse IgG heavy-chain MAF. Ig-Seq and Rep-Seq remain broader names, with the separately cited Vollmers implementation supported here only at abstract level. The CDR3 key is descriptive; no alternative material branch is drawn. Sequencing and computational correction are described only as supported downstream readout interfaces.

states.label: Extracted RNA: rearranged immunoglobulin transcripts
features: The labelled target contains V, D, J and Constant regions. The separate left key highlights the CDR3 junction region; it is a descriptive target map, not another material stream.
The illustrated input is RNA, despite the grouped caption mentioning DNA sequencing. The paper-supported MAF implementation targets mouse IgG heavy-chain transcripts.
Dotted strand continuations indicate omitted extent; no specific terminal chemical group, surface attachment or cell compartment is identified.

states.label: DNA: purified, tagged immunoglobulin sequencing library
features: The final labelled DNA product follows Purify. DNA is the sequenced carrier of the original RNA-derived immunoglobulin sequence and RID/FID associations.

In paper-supported MAF, Illumina sequencing supplies reads for RID-based consensus, VDJ/CDR3 repertoire characterization and FID/RID-based amplification-bias correction. Sequencing and computation are downstream interfaces, not additional operations drawn here.

The library supports transcript-derived sequence diversity and relative abundance estimates. RNA abundance does not directly establish the number of cells expressing a clone; the bulk workflow does not preserve native VH:VL pairing.

operations.information_effect: Moves immunoglobulin transcript sequence information onto DNA and associates that cDNA with an RID; the input RNA serves as template.

method_scopes.rationale: The catalogue explicitly identifies the drawing as MAF. Khan et al. describe RNA-to-RID cDNA, multiplex PCR adding FIDs, and adapter extension PCR. The diagram's Second strand synthesis boundary is retained as the early forward extension within multiplex amplification; its PCR block is broad. Literal 8N labels are corrected to the paper's spacer-containing, partially degenerate UIDs. The specifically evidenced implementation is mouse IgG heavy-chain MAF, not all possible immunoglobulin or T-cell-receptor protocols.

method_scopes.rationale: Ig-Seq is the broader immunoglobulin-sequencing application, within which MAF is a specific preparation/correction approach. The catalogue-listed Vollmers study is a distinct RNA-barcode/consensus implementation: its supplied abstract supports labelling starting RNA molecules and estimating RNA/isotype levels, but does not establish the MAF RID/FID scheme or map its reaction stages to this drawing. The catalogue's gDNA-to-cDNA wording does not alter the diagram's explicitly RNA-derived route. No figure operation is assigned universally to Ig-Seq.

Interpreting the depicted second-strand stage as the early forward-primer extension within that multiplex amplification reconciles the boundary without claiming an independently reported reaction.

unknowns.question: Which, if any, of the separate second-strand, dual-UID and PCR stages in the MAF drawing apply to the specific Vollmers et al. Ig-Seq implementation? Its supplied abstract establishes starting-RNA barcoding and consensus readout but not reaction order or primer architecture; its full library-preparation methods/figure would be needed to resolve that mapping.
